html:
SMTO-EXE-0199 — This file isn't a complete, readable PDF

GUID: a4ebce1b-cbe9-59e8-8831-55a810f63ab4
Slug: pdf-invalid-pdf
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • SMTO checked the file and it doesn't look like a complete, well-formed PDF, so it stopped without making anything. Your original file was not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the file in your usual PDF viewer on that computer and check that every page displays. If a normal viewer can't open it either, the file itself is damaged or incomplete.
  2. If the file was downloaded, emailed or copied, get it again and make sure the transfer finished. A partly copied file is missing its ending, which SMTO checks for.
  3. Check that the file really is a PDF and not another kind of file renamed to end in .pdf. Renaming a file doesn't change its contents, so SMTO still can't read it as a PDF.
  4. If you have the original document, export or save it as a new PDF, keep the old file, and give SMTO the new one. A freshly made PDF fixes broken structure without SMTO guessing at repairs.

What success looks like

  • SMTO can report the page count of the new PDF and completes the action you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying where the PDF came from. Keep the original file; don't overwrite it while testing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Strict PDF parsing on the Gateway rejected the file: missing %PDF- header or %%EOF marker, malformed structure, invalid page size or user unit, or another parser error.

What this means

  • Strict parsing rejected missing PDF header/end marker, malformed structure, invalid page dimensions/user unit or another parser exception not mapped to a specific bound. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • Strict parsing rejected missing PDF header/end marker, malformed structure, invalid page dimensions/user unit or another parser exception not mapped to a specific bound.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect structural failure evidence and source completeness; preserve the original instead of silently applying parser repair.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the file on the Gateway: it must start with '%PDF-' and have '%%EOF' in its last 1024 bytes, and every page MediaBox width/height and /UserUnit must be finite and between 0 and 100000. The worker uses pypdf strict=True and never repairs files silently; provide a complete valid PDF (for example re-exported from the source application) and keep the original untouched.
  • Use a complete valid PDF and inspect its structure; preserve the original and avoid silent parser repair.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a complete valid PDF. No output was published; parser repair is not silently attempted.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid supported PDF passes strict bounded inspection before output generation.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
